item.title: Storm affects two dozen flights to/from Springfield airport
item.description: SPRINGFIELD, Mo. – By midmorning today, 22 flights to or from Springfield-Branson International Airport have been canceled by the winter storm raging across the country this weekend. item.title: Deep cold forecast prompts city to postpone council meeting
item.description: SPRINGFIELD, Mo. – Monday night’s Springfield City Council meeting has been postponed due to anticipated extreme cold temperatures. The meeting is rescheduled for 6:30 p.m. Feb. 2 at the Springfield Regional Police & Fire Training Center at 2620 W. Battlefield Road. item.title: How long will snow stay on the ground? Latest forecast details
item.description: Schools and businesses in Springfield, Missouri have been closed due to over half a foot of snow, and while temperatures are expected to rise to around 32 degrees on Tuesday, another arctic cold front is expected to arrive by the end of the week, meaning snow will likely remain on the ground for at least another week.

item.title: City & County crews working to clear priority roads
item.description: City and county crews are working to clear roads and highways of snow in Springfield and Greene County, prioritizing heavily used areas and advising drivers to keep their distance from snow removal trucks.

item.title: Winter storm aftermath: Extreme cold creating subzero conditions
item.description: The Ozarks have been hit with a winter storm, leaving behind half a foot of snow and subzero temperatures, with wind chills as low as -20 degrees, and only mild temperatures expected to return by the end of the week.

item.title: City Utilities provides tips to lower your winter bill and ease demand
item.description: City Utilities encourages customers to take simple steps to lower their winter bill and ease demand, such as setting their thermostat to 68°F, delaying major energy-consuming activities, limiting non-essential appliances and electronics, and minimizing heating and lighting in empty rooms.

item.title: List of warming centers for impending winter storm
item.description: Warming centers and cold weather shelters are opening up across the Ozarks due to forecasted freezing temperatures and negative wind chills, with a list of shelters and warming centers available on the CPO website and the Missouri Department of Health & Senior Services website.
